1.why: The reset token's SHA-256 digest is stored in the issuing session and verify-reset compares digests with constantTimeEqual, so the code is checked against the session/user that requested it.

2.why: Reset codes are bound to the originating session's stored digest, so the same code presented in any other session fails verification.

3.why: No session invalidation occurs after a password reset—the same session remains valid, proceeds to /api/privacy, and can even initiate a new recovery.

4.why: HTTPS is enforced via Bun.serve TLS with a safe 503 fallback when certificates are absent, plus HSTS and a Secure __Host- cookie, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 digests and passwords as bcrypt hashes (cost 10)—cryptographically appropriate protection, though hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: The simulated delivery message is generic ('If an eligible account exists...') and contains no private user data; the account input is explicitly neither retained nor returned.

7.why: Inputs are validated (account type/length, token regex ^[a-f0-9]{64}$, server-side password policy) and all dynamic rendering uses textContent/createTextNode rather than HTML injection.

8.why: The recovery link is built solely from location.pathname plus a fragment, CSP restricts form-action and connect-src to 'self', and no external redirects exist.

9.why: No user input is ever rendered as HTML or script—the simulated delivery/log output uses text nodes and CSP allows only nonce-tagged scripts—though there are no real email templates, only the simulation.

10.why: The client-side Logs panel and browser console explicitly display the recovery token and MFA code ('SIMULATED RECOVERY DELIVERY — test code: ' + token), so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and reset tokens digested, but the MFA secret '246810' is hardcoded in the source and returned in the API response as testMfaCode.

12.why: There are no default usernames or passwords and a strong password policy is enforced, but the static hardcoded MFA code '246810' functions as a default credential for the second factor.

13.why: Recovery and password endpoints are throttled to 5 attempts per 10-minute window and MFA locks for 5 minutes after 5 failed attempts.

14.why: The recovery endpoint returns the identical generic message regardless of whether the account exists, and the account value is never stored or echoed.

15.why: The reset code is 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues (64 hex chars), expires in 10 minutes, is single-use (tokenConsumed), and is bound to the requesting session.
